Diabetes is an independent risk factor for macrovascular 
disease in addition to the common coexisting risk factors of 
hypertension and dyslipidemia (see Chapter 13). Hypertension
is not only a major risk factor for CVD, but also a complication
for microvascular complications of DM such as retinopathy 
and nephropathy. Hypertension is often the consequence of 
underlying nephropathy in individuals with T1DM. In T2DM, 
hypertension may manifest as part of the metabolic syndrome
(see Chapter 13), which is accompanied by high rates of CVD. 
Hypertension can be improved by increasing physical activ-
ity and consumption of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy 
products; by decreasing sodium intake and body weight
(when indicated); and by avoiding excessive alcohol intake.
Dyslipidemia can be improved by a reduction of saturated fat 
and cholesterol intake, weight loss if indicated, and increased
physical activity.11
